data.why: CesiumAstro made multiple acquisitions in August, which directly impacts the Corporate Controller responsible for integrating disparate ledgers. Focusing on the operational burden of folding new companies into the close creates an immediate and relevant reason to reach out.
data.angle: Reconciling purchase orders, supplier invoices, and separate general ledgers during the month-end close across newly acquired companies.

not_chosen.reason: The Series D round dollar amount conflicts across sources ($630M vs $730M), and generic funding is less relevant to close operations than acquisitions.
This is a job posting for the prospect's own title (Corporate Controller), which would be awkward to mention.
Opening a Florida manufacturing facility is strong, but integrating completed acquisitions creates a more direct accounting close headache for a Controller.
Hiring for SEC reporting is focused on technical reporting rather than back-office accounting operations and close workflows.
Headcount growth (+60%) is a generic metric that lacks the specific operational friction of recent acquisitions.

data.subject: recent acquisitions
data.body:
Hi Sanjiv,

CesiumAstro picked up 1Aardvark and Jariet Technologies in August. Bringing acquired teams into one accounting close usually means days of sorting through new purchase orders and matching supplier invoices across separate sets of books. Who is keying those in today?

Block cut 75% of the manual steps in its close with Zamp.

Worth a look before year-end?

[Your name]
